title: Keep it, cash it or consolidate
outcomes: Chooses between keeping the initiative, cashing it in and consolidating
Asks what the opponent threatens before spending a tempo on an attack
Recognises a position where nobody has an initiative to keep

steps.text: In **Who is making the threats?** you listed threats and the replies they force. Now decide what to do with an initiative. You can **keep up** the threats, **cash in** by turning the pressure into material, or **consolidate** by answering his threat first. Two questions decide it: if I pass, what can he do? And is anything of his loose?

**Rule of thumb:** cash in when the material is free and the capture does not trade off your attackers. Keep up when a capture would only trade the pieces that make the threats. Consolidate when his threat is faster than yours. A quiet move that adds a threat keeps the initiative. In the next three positions the same White pieces face three different jobs.

steps.title: Same pieces, three jobs
steps.prompt: White is to move in each position. Predict whether the best plan is to keep up the threats, to cash in the material, or to consolidate by answering his threat first. Then check.

steps.text: No labels now. Some positions reward more pressure, some a safe capture, and one has no initiative to keep. The next four exercises are silent.

steps.prompt: Think of a game of yours where you had the initiative. Did you keep it, cash it in or consolidate? Which of the two questions (what can he do if I pass, is anything of his loose) would have helped?
